questions.question: How many official languages does the United Nations have?
questions.explanation: The UN has six official languages - Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian, and Spanish - but English serves as the primary working language.

questions.question: What role does English play at the United Nations in practice?
options: It is the primary working language for most UN business
It is banned in the General Assembly
It is used only for translation
It was replaced by French in 1990
questions.explanation: Although six languages are official, English dominates day-to-day UN work, drafting, and informal negotiation.

questions.question: What is a "resolution" in diplomatic language?
options: A formal decision or expression of will adopted by an international body
questions.explanation: In diplomacy, a resolution is a formal text adopted by a body like the UN Security Council or General Assembly expressing a decision or position.

questions.question: Why is diplomatic language typically cautious and indirect?
options: To maintain relationships and avoid escalation while still conveying positions
questions.explanation: Diplomatic English uses careful, measured phrasing - expressing "concern" or "regret" - to signal positions without closing doors to negotiation.

questions.question: When was the United Nations founded, and how many member states does it have?
questions.explanation: The UN was founded in 1945 after World War II and today has 193 member states.
